hypothesis: A hardcoded lr=3e-4 is a GPT-2-scale constant (width 768-1600) and is far below the optimum for this rig's width (256). A width-appropriate LR reaches a materially lower train loss at equal step count.
why_train_loss_endpoint: The corpus builder's train/val split is positional, so training text can appear verbatim in validation. Any val-based endpoint is therefore untrustworthy until the split is made group-aware. Train loss sidesteps the problem entirely.

fixed_config.schedule: cosine with 5% warmup, min_lr = lr/10 (train.py's cosine_lr, unchanged)
fixed_config.optimizer: AdamW betas=(0.9,0.95) wd=0.1, grad clip 1.0 (train.py's, unchanged)

stage_1_sweep.purpose: locate the optimum LR at this width; single seed, NOT the confirmatory test
stage_1_sweep.treatment_selection_rule: the LR with the lowest final train loss becomes the treatment arm. Declared BEFORE running so the choice is mechanical, not eyeballed.

stage_2_confirm.endpoint: final train loss, measured on 40 FIXED eval batches drawn from a dedicated torch.Generator(seed=12345) so every arm and seed sees byte-identical eval batches, and evaluation can never perturb the training stream

success_bar.primary: mean(control train loss) - mean(treatment train loss) >= 0.020
success_bar.secondary: zero overlap between the two arms' 5-seed [min,max] ranges

prespecified_outcomes.pass: both bars met -> a fixed lr=3e-4 default is wrong for this width; scale the LR with width rather than hand-tuning a new constant.
prespecified_outcomes.fail: gap < 0.020 or ranges overlap -> report as null. Do NOT re-run with different steps/width and report the winner; a second run is a NEW preregistration.
prespecified_outcomes.surprise: if control WINS, report that plainly — it falsifies the hypothesis on this rig and that is a result worth having.

not_claimed: That this generalizes to other depths. This runs 4 layers and does not re-measure the scaling law at each depth.
That train loss is a proxy for model quality. It is the endpoint because val is not yet trustworthy, not because it is the better measure.
That the resulting LR is optimal at any width other than the one measured (256).
